summary.headline: Greenlam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to INR797 crore, with EBITDA before forex up 48% to INR81 crore and net profit of INR21 crore versus a loss a year earlier.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 18% YoY to about INR797 crore, while gross margin held near 53% (52.9%) despite sharp input and freight cost increases. EBITDA before forex rose 48% to INR81 crore, with margin up 210 bps to 10.2%, and net profit turned positive at INR21 crore against a INR15.5 crore loss last year. Laminates grew 7% but volumes fell 6% because about INR27 crore of export shipments slipped into Q2 due to container and vessel constraints from the West Asia conflict. The chipboard business turned EBITDA positive for the first time, and plywood losses narrowed. Management reiterated FY27 laminate revenue growth of 10-12% and total revenue growth target of 18%, but gave no visibility on freight or raw material normalisation.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: Revenue INR596 crore, +7% YoY; sales volume 4.62 million sheets (-6% YoY) on export postponement; production 4.9 million sheets at 80% utilisation. EBITDA margin before forex 13.9% (+70 bps). Realisation INR1,240 per sheet, +14% YoY.

segments.name: Plywood and Allied
segments.commentary: Revenue INR106 crore, +20% YoY; EBITDA loss before forex narrowed to INR5 crore from INR9 crore. Plywood sales 1.66 million sq m (+19% YoY), realisation INR276 per sq m (+4%), utilisation 39% vs 28%. Engineered floors and doors together INR29 crore revenue with EBITDA loss of INR1.2 crore.

segments.name: Panel and Allied (chipboard)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR95 crore, nearly 4x YoY; EBITDA before forex INR3.4 crore vs loss of INR10 crore a year earlier. Sales volume 41,418 cubic metres (+167% YoY); realisation INR22,764 per CBM (+15%); utilisation 61% vs 30%.

guidance_outlook: Total revenue growth target of 18% for FY27 reiterated; management expects to achieve it but gave no volume/value split.
Laminate revenue growth guided at 10-12% for FY27, despite Q1 at about 7%; management said it is difficult to guide quarterly volume or margin given raw material uncertainty.
Plywood utilisation expected near 50% for FY27 (about 40% in Q1); EBITDA breakeven targeted within FY27, with timing uncertain; PAT breakeven may slip to FY28.
Chipboard utilisation expected to average about 70% in FY27; 18-20% EBITDA margin possible at full utilisation and better mix, expected around FY29.
FY27 capex budget INR130-135 crore including about INR70 crore for laminate expansion; no large new capacity planned beyond the announced laminate lines.
Debt expected to fall by about INR100 crore in FY27; FY28 repayments slightly above INR150 crore as per schedule, with stronger debt reduction thereafter as capex eases.
capex_capacity: Two new laminate press lines on track for commercial production by Q4 FY27; equipment already ordered, mostly domestic.
Laminate capacity addition aimed at specific categories already near optimum utilisation (laminate at 80% in Q1).
No plan for large capacity addition beyond the laminate lines; FY27 is a year of sweating existing assets.
Chipboard: sufficient capacity for now; management said pre-laminate share will rise as utilisation approaches 80-90%, with any new capacity decision after that, roughly 4-5 quarters away.
Peak utilisation views: laminate and chipboard up to 100%; plywood 85-100% over time; decorative veneer, floors and doors 60-65%.
demand_pricing: Domestic laminate volume fell about 7.5% YoY as real estate and project customers delayed dispatches amid building material cost increases; retail and distribution held up.
Export shipments of about INR27 crore moved from Q1 to Q2 due to container and vessel shortages and longer transit times; Middle East is about 6-7% of business.

Price hikes in April and May on chemicals (about one-third of raw material cost; up to 35% of laminate and chipboard content); partial price cuts in June and July. Net pass-through was 7-8% of the increase.
Plywood price increased modestly in April in phases, with the pass-through limited because chemical content is low; plywood realisation about INR270-275 per sq m.
Chipboard realisation INR22,764 per CBM; management sees headroom through pre-laminate and HMR premium products.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price cuts cause destocking in the trade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stock is held on demand rather than pushed into channels, so no negative impact is expected; lower prices should help secondary demand.

qa_highlights.question: Will plywood reach EBITDA breakeven, and in which quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven is targeted within FY27, but management said it would be a single quarter, not the full year; PAT breakeven may follow in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the laminate volume decline not reflected in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10-12% guidance is on revenue; adding back about INR30 crore of deferred exports brings volume close to the target, and it still stands by the range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR135 crore net (INR70 crore laminate, INR40 crore maintenance, INR10-20 crore past payments), with debt expected to fall about INR100 crore; FY28 repayments are above INR150 crore per schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Is chipboard capacity enough, and when is more needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is sufficient; management will move toward pre-laminate mix and will decide on new capacity once utilisation nears 80-90%.

qa_highlights.question: Plywood target of about INR20 per sq m EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR20 per sq m equals about 8-8.5% EBITDA, achievable only at 80-90% utilisation over time; current realisation is about INR270-275 per sq m.

risks_watch: Export timing: about INR27 crore of shipments slipped from Q1 into Q2; management said it could not predict whether container and vessel constraints would persist for the full quarter, and a full-quarter continuation would hit export sales.

Laminate guidance: FY27 laminate revenue growth of 10-12% is reiterated despite Q1 volume down 6% and Q1 revenue growth of about 7%; management gave no quarterly volume or margin guidance because of raw material uncertainty.

Raw material volatility: chemicals (about one-third of raw material cost, up to 35% of laminate and chipboard content) moved up, down and up again; management said the picture is hazy and gave no freight or raw material normalisation view.

Domestic project demand: domestic laminate volume fell about 7.5% YoY as real estate and project customers delayed dispatches; management expects demand to improve with more market clarity but gave no timing.

Plywood breakeven: EBITDA breakeven is targeted within FY27 but would be a single quarter, timing unspecified; PAT breakeven may slip to FY28. Plywood utilisation is about 39-40% against a FY27 expectation of around 50%.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year revenue target and laminate growth range, but cautious and often non-committal on quarterly volume, margins, raw material direction, export timing and plywood breakeven timing. Several answers were deferred ("we will touch base offline") and the call was briefly interrupted when the management line dropped.

adds.what: Two new laminate press lines (laminate expansion, part of ~INR70 crore FY27 laminate capex)

growth.why: Management reiterated 18% consolidated FY27 revenue growth and 10-12% laminate growth, with two laminate press lines due by Q4 FY27 and laminate at 80% utilisation; but Q1 revenue grew only 18% with laminate volume down 6%, and no large new capacity is planned, so outlook is positive but not strongly capacity-backed.
